value-in-db: coal-methanol 2.60 GJ/t (0-2.60); its ccs variant 6.18; coal-ammonia 6.91 (0.68-16.5)
issue: The feedstock rule (pipeline/feedstock.py, threshold 0.9 x product energy) subtracts the product's energy from IEA 2013 Annex 4 Table 5 values whose own note says the SEC EXCLUDES feedstock: iea_2013_001-0149 24.0 to 2.60 and -0151 20.1 to 0 on coal methanol, -0011 27.92 to 6.91 and -0013 22.00 to 0.68 on coal ammonia. The rule fires on size alone, so the feed comes off twice. This is the root cause of open item S126.
benchmark: IEA 2013 Table 5 as printed: coal methanol 24 (average) and 20.1 (BPT) GJ/t, coal ammonia 27.9 and 22 GJ/t, all feed-excluded LHV, so about 25-30 GJ/t on HHV; IEA 2021 coal ammonia BAT 36 GJ/t net incl. 34 GJ coal (about 15 GJ/t after the feed comes off).
recommendation: Exempt feed-excluded rows from the take-off: add a per-example or per-source flag (for example an exclusion column in records/reference/feedstock.csv keyed on iea_2013_001 Table 5) and skip rows whose note says the SEC excludes feedstock. Rebuild and re-check S126.

issue: The carrier split takes Boulamanti 2017 (boulamanti_2017_001:gasifier_coal-ammonia, Sect. 5.2.2), which reports only electricity (3.7 GJ/t), as a 100% share of the pooled total, so the whole (already wrong) total is labelled electricity. The coal carrier, 21.9 GJ/t from Rouwenhorst 2019, then sits outside the total.
benchmark: Boulamanti 2017: 3.7 GJ/t electricity for coal ammonia; the rest of the 15-30 GJ/t is coal.
recommendation: Do not use an example that reports a single carrier as a 100% share of a multi-carrier total; keep electricity at the example's own 3.7 GJ/t and give the remainder to coal. The same defect shows on reactor_chemical-depolymerization (CHEM014).

value-in-db: 31.17 GJ/t on both (total 31.67 and 34.28) beside feedstock-consumption 22.48
issue: Martin 2000 (martin_2000_001 p.81, Chemicals-7) prints 26.8 MBtu/short-ton of fuel for ATR ammonia, which is the whole gas use including feed. The feedstock rule only checks rows tagged with the feed carrier (natural-gas) or untagged, so this 'fuel' row keeps the feed, and the archetype then adds 22.48 GJ/t of feedstock on top: 53.6 GJ/t of gas per t ammonia.
benchmark: Modern ATR ammonia uses 28-32 GJ/t of gas in total (JRC 2007 Table 2.6: 31.8 GJ/t net LHV, feed 24.8), so fuel about 5-9 GJ/t once the 22.48 GJ/t feed is off.
recommendation: Let the take-off also test 'fuel' rows on archetypes whose feed is the fuel (natural-gas on reformers), or tag Martin's row natural-gas; the ATR fuel should land near 5-9 GJ/t. Re-run the ccs variant, which inherits the value.

issue: DEA 2026 (dea_2026_003 sheet 95) gives 1.724 MWh biomass per MWh methanol, the whole biomass input including the part that ends in the product. It is tagged biomass-solid, while records/reference/feedstock.csv lists only 'biomass' as the feed for this archetype, so the take-off skips it; the fill then adds 22.66 GJ/t of feedstock again. The archetype's own efficiency (62.7%) implies about 32 GJ/t of biomass in total, not 59.
benchmark: Total biomass about 31-36 GJ/t HHV per t methanol (DEA 2026; efficiency 54-70%), so SEC after the feed is off about 9-14 GJ/t.
recommendation: Add biomass-solid (and fuel) to the feed list for gasifier_biomass-methanol, as fermenter_lignocellulosic-enzymatic already does, and rebuild.

issue: The est-sibling-capacity rule fills every chlor-alkali and chlorate cell from electrolysis-cell_prebaked-anode, an aluminium smelter whose only example (jrc_2026_001) is EU output over capacity in 2023, depressed by the 2022-23 curtailments. A curtailed smelter is the wrong analogue for a chlor-alkali cell room, and the low factor more than doubles the capital part of the levelized cost (membrane cost-levelized 1468 CAD/t) and cuts annual output to 252 kt on a 640 kt/yr plant.
benchmark: Chlor-alkali plants run at about 80-90% of capacity (Euro Chlor utilisation about 80-85% in normal years).
recommendation: Require the sibling rule to match the duty (same product or end use) before borrowing a capacity factor, or fall back to the class median; set chlor-alkali near 85%. Also tell the non-ferrous reviewer that the smelter's 39.4% is a crisis-year figure.

value-in-db: captured 0.647 t/t (0.496-0.996); share-to-capture 100% (derived); net emissions-total 0.068 t/t
issue: The captured pool takes UKERC CH-SC30 to CH-SC33, which are post-combustion capture on natural-gas and biomass boilers, beside the cracker rows CH-SC34 to CH-SC37, all read from 'kg/unit' as t per t HVC. The median, 0.647 t/t, is 90% of the host's whole CO2 (0.715), so the derived share-to-capture comes out at 101%, is clipped to 100%, and replaces the sourced 83% and 90%. Net emissions end up 90% below the host.
benchmark: Johansson 2012: furnace flue gas is 83% of site CO2; DOE 2023: 90% capture rate. Captured about 0.9 x 0.83 x 0.715 = 0.53 t/t, net about 0.18 t/t.
recommendation: Drop the boiler rows from the cracker's capture pool, check the UKERC per-unit basis (per t ethylene or HVC), and compute captured as capture rate x furnace share x host CO2; keep share-to-capture at the furnace share (about 75-83%).

issue: Emission factors stated per unit of FUEL input in a non-GJ unit skip the efficiency bridge and pool as per GJ of output. normalise.py (line 465) sets the per-input bridge only when the raw unit ends in /GJ, so EIA 2024 lb/MMBtu rows (tp-eia_2024_001-0041, -0008, -0025, -0057), DOE 2024 t/MMBtu (tp-doe_2024_002-0022) and Zuhlsdorf 2019 kg/MWh of fuel (tp-zuhlsdorf_2019_001-0047) go through unconverted. combined-cycle's only sourced CO2 value is the natural-gas emission factor itself.
benchmark: Per GJ of electricity: CCGT at 49% HHV about 0.10 t/GJ; ultra-supercritical coal at 40% about 0.22 t/GJ; per GJ of boiler heat at 81% about 0.062 t/GJ.
recommendation: Apply the per-input bridge to any energy denominator (MMBtu, MWh, kWh, J) when the record says fuel input, or add an explicit input-basis flag to the extraction rows and bridge on it. Re-run and recheck combined-cycle, its ccs variant, and steam-turbine_condensing.

value-in-db: no emissions-total row; emissions-combustion 0.0502988 t/GJ (estimated, host copy); emissions-captured 0.100389
issue: The capture variant has no net emissions-total, against the ruling. ccs-host-emissions needs a host emissions-total and combined-cycle has only emissions-combustion, so the rule does not fire. The copied host value is the fuel-basis factor from HPCH001, so captured CO2 (Irlam 2017, tp-irlam_2017_001-0076) is twice the host's 'gross'. The sourced net rows (Irlam 0.0111, tp-irlam_2017_001-0074) are not used.
benchmark: Host gross about 0.10 t/GJ electricity; at 90-95% capture, net 0.005-0.011 t/GJ (Irlam 2017 prints 40 kg/MWh = 0.011).
recommendation: After the HPCH001 fix, let ccs-host-emissions fall back to the host's emissions-combustion when the host has no emissions-total, and write the net emissions-total for the variant.

issue: The rule computes net as host gross less the sourced emissions-captured and floors the result at zero without a warning. On these three variants the captured CO2 comes from a different plant than the host and exceeds the host's gross: 0.121 vs 0.066 (boiler), 0.0622 vs 0.0493 (ATR), 0.131 vs 0.120 (coal gasifier). The variants then show zero net emissions despite share-to-capture of 90%, 94.5%, and 100%.
benchmark: Net = host gross x (1 - share-to-capture): boiler about 0.0066, ATR about 0.0027, coal gasifier about 0.012 t/GJ at 90% capture.
recommendation: When the sourced captured exceeds the host gross, take emissions-captured = share-to-capture x host gross (and report the conflict in the review file) rather than clipping net to zero. Also check whether a 100% share-to-capture on the coal gasifier is right; 90% is typical.

value-in-db: efficiency 56.8673 % (low 56.87, high 95); emissions-captured 0.12086 t/GJ (high 0.2317); carriers include coal, nuclear, biomass
issue: A gas-boiler capture variant pools a coal CFB boiler (IEAGHG 2007 case 3, tp-ieaghg_2007_001-0043 and -0048) and a steel works-gas boiler (IEAGHG 2013, tp-ieaghg_2013_003-0176). The central efficiency is the coal plant's net of regeneration heat, while the reboiler steam is already a separate SEC carrier, so the penalty is counted twice. HP013 (2026-10-11) raised the carrier side; the build still shows it.
benchmark: Gas boiler with capture: boiler efficiency stays near the host's 81-85% with reboiler steam as its own carrier; captured about 0.9 x 0.062 = 0.056 t/GJ heat.
recommendation: Re-map the coal CFB example to a solid-fuel boiler capture variant (or exclude it here) and the works-gas boiler to the steel family; re-pool efficiency and emissions-captured on gas-fired examples only.

value-in-db: efficiency 18.85 % (est-sibling-efficiency); SEC 5.30504 GJ/GJ (inverse), against a guessed geothermal carrier of 1.05
issue: After the HP009 fix removed the DEA heat-pump COPs, est-sibling-efficiency now fills the efficiency from the binary and flash POWER plants (tier 2), because the rule matches on product unit (GJ) and not on product (heat vs electricity). The SEC then inherits a power-plant conversion of about 5x, and the archetype's own carrier split (geothermal 1.05) contradicts it.
benchmark: Direct-use heat exchange delivers most of the brine heat: geothermal SEC 1.0-1.2 GJ/GJ (the archetype's own guess), efficiency about 85-95% or not applicable.
recommendation: Restrict est-sibling-efficiency to siblings with the same product, not only the same product unit. Fill this archetype from a guess near 90% or leave the efficiency not applicable.

value-in-db: 0.78945 GJ/GJ (proxy, est-bucket-saving-sec); efficiency 95.0029 % copied from the host
issue: The bucket rule applies the strong saving (25%) to the host SEC of 1.0526 and gives 0.789 GJ of fuel per GJ of heat, which implies 127% efficiency. The variant's efficiency is the host's 95% unchanged, so the two parameters disagree and the SEC breaks the first law.
benchmark: A combustion heater cannot go below 1.0 GJ/GJ; with the host at 95% there is at most about 5% left to save.
recommendation: Bound est-bucket-saving-sec so the result never falls below 100 / (maximum efficiency), or derive the saving from the gap to the bound; recompute the efficiency from the reduced SEC so the two agree.

value-in-db: SEC 0.29379 GJ/GJ; emissions-combustion co2 -0.0407306 t/GJ; emissions-total co2e -0.0722632
issue: All three rest on one UKERC PP-CHP1 measure row ('Use of wastes with gasification', tp-ukerc_2013_001-0150 and -0153), stated per unit of the baseline output. These are changes against a baseline, not the gasifier's own use, and a biomass CHP cannot use 0.29 GJ of fuel per GJ of heat or have negative combustion emissions.
benchmark: Total efficiency 77% (the archetype's own value): about 1.3 GJ biomass per GJ of total output, about 2-2.5 GJ per GJ of heat at a heat-to-power ratio of 2.25; combustion CO2 biogenic, so fossil emissions-combustion near zero and the rest in emissions-biomass.
recommendation: Exclude the UKERC PP-CHP1 SEC and emissions rows (or treat them as measure deltas); fill SEC from the efficiency identity.

archetype: coke-oven_by-product_efficiency-moderate; blast-furnace_efficiency-moderate; basic-oxygen-furnace_efficiency-strong; electric-arc-furnace_scrap-preheating; sinter-plant_efficiency-moderate; sinter-plant_efficiency-strong
value-in-db: coke-oven eff-moderate 6.62 GJ/t against host 4.01; blast-furnace eff-moderate 13.1 against host 16.5
issue: The UKERC saving rows apply each saving to a stale host total. build.py calls ukercsaving.derive (line 161) before carriers.example_totals (line 167), so the base total omits every carrier-derived total added on 2026-10-21. tp-epa_2012_001-s001 reads 'coke-oven_by-product's pooled total SEC 6.864', but the host now pools 4.008; the blast-furnace rows use 13.63 (host now 16.50), the BOF row 0.1787 (now 0.457), and the EAF row 3.051 (now 2.224). As a result the moderate coke-oven bucket uses 65% more energy than its host, and the moderate blast-furnace bucket shows a 20% saving where UKERC gives about 4%.
benchmark: Variant = current host total x (1 - UKERC saving): coke-oven about 3.8-3.9 GJ/t, blast furnace about 15.8 GJ/t
recommendation: Move the ukercsaving.derive call after carriers.example_totals in build.py, or recompute the base from the final pooled host, and add a check that fails when a derived-from-base row's base differs from the host's pooled central.

issue: carriers.example_totals summed a partial carrier table into a whole-furnace total. tp-remus_2013_001-0034-total (Remus 2013 IS BREF p.304 Table 6.1) is only the stove fuels (BFG 1.57, COG 0.32, NG 0.19, BOF gas 0.22), electricity, and steam, with no coke or PCI, yet it pools as a 2.62 GJ/t blast-furnace total. It sets the low band, and because the carrier bands scale from the total, it drags every carrier low down too (coke low 1.93, coal low 0.63), and with them the efficiency and ccs variants. This is the S117 risk realised in the derived-total step.
benchmark: Blast-furnace total 12-19 GJ/t hot metal (Remus Table 6.16 19.4, IEAGHG 16.7, Worrell 1999 13.8)
recommendation: Exclude tp-remus_2013_001-0034-total. In carriers.example_totals, skip an example whose carriers do not include the archetype's main carrier (coke or coal for the blast furnace), or flag example totals below 0.3x the pooled median for review. Check the other low derived totals that may be partial too: tp-ieaghg_2013_003-0117-total (caster 0.058), tp-ieaghg_2013_003-0115-total (ladle 0.108), tp-remus_2013_001-0055-total (BOF 0.134), and tp-ieaghg_2013_003-0078-total (sinter 0.197).

issue: The pool mixes mill-only and mill-plus-reheat-furnace scopes. NRCan 2007 (tp-nrcan_2007_001-0041, 'mill fuel 1229 less furnace fuel 1010 MJ/t'), Worrell 2010, and DOE 2000 give 0.3-0.5 GJ/t for the mill. DOE 2015 (1.86, 3.0), Worrell 1999 (3.96), Daniels 2002 (2.05), and Hasanbeigi ('includes reheating') include the reheating furnace. Reheating is its own CIMS node (iron-and-steel.service.reheating, furnace_reheating 1.84 GJ/t), so the central counts reheat fuel twice. The guessed natural-gas 1.50 GJ/t and the combustion CO2 0.076 t/t follow from the same fuel.
benchmark: Hot mill without reheating: about 0.3-0.5 GJ/t, mostly electricity (NRCan 2007 App. A; Worrell 2010 Table 4-1)
recommendation: Per the node-scope ruling, keep only mill-scope rows on rolling-mill_hot. Exclude or rebase the whole-line rows (doe_2015_001-0022/-0023, worrell_1999_001-0013/-0021, daniels_2002_001-0112, hasanbeigi_2013_001-0006) or subtract the reheat furnace. Reject the natural-gas judgement. The same applies to rolling-mill_hot_efficiency-moderate.

value-in-db: total 1.65 GJ/t, fuel 1.22, natural-gas 1.22 (guess), low 0.068, high 4.05
issue: The fuel on the cold mill is annealing and finishing fuel. Worrell 1999 (tp-worrell_1999_001-0015) is 'cold rolling and finishing', and DOE 2000 (tp-doe_2000_001-0037) says 'possibly annealing fuel'. The DOE 2015 totals 1.65 and 4.05 are also whole cold-mill complex. Annealing has its own node (annealing-and-coating, annealing-furnace_* 0.9-1.0 GJ/t), so the fuel is counted twice. JRC 2022 (tp-jrc_2022_001-0030 to -0034) gives 65-550 MJ/t for most mills, and Daniels gives 0 GJ/t gas.
benchmark: Cold mill alone: 0.3-0.6 GJ/t, almost all electricity (JRC 2022 FMP BREF Table 3.3; Daniels 2002 Table 2.22)
recommendation: Exclude the fuel rows that include annealing, or rebase them, and pool the total on mill-only rows. Then the natural-gas guess and the 0.062 t/t combustion CO2 drop away. Check rolling-mill_cold_efficiency-moderate, which is scaled from this host.

value-in-db: hydrogen 4.61 GJ/t, natural-gas 3.48 GJ/t, fuel 8.09, total 8.92
issue: Hydrogen sits below every hydrogen example (Devlin 6.82, Otto 8.01, and Rechberger 8.09 GJ/t) and below the reduction stoichiometry. The fuel row (Rechberger 635 m3 H2/t, tp-rechberger_2020_001-0013) is split 57/43 hydrogen/natural gas using Otto 2017's Circored case, which fires natural gas for heat (tp-otto_2017_001-0028, 6.05 GJ/t NG). That puts 3.5 GJ/t of gas and 0.176 t/t combustion CO2 on a hydrogen archetype, against the archetype's own emissions-total of 0.04 t/t. The carriers also sum to 13.5 GJ/t against the 8.92 total (screen-carriers).
benchmark: About 50-55 kg H2/t DRI, so 7-8 GJ/t HHV, with natural gas at most about 0.5 GJ/t (Rechberger 2020 Sect. 2: 48-50 m3/t)
recommendation: Do not split the Rechberger fuel by Otto's Circored shares. Read tp-rechberger_2020_001-0013 as hydrogen, as its target already says. Take natural gas from Rechberger's 48-50 m3/t once those rows convert (next finding), or set Otto's natural-gas heating row aside as IS020 did for the electrolytic route.

issue: The coke dry quenching (CDQ) add-on cost pools as if it were the whole plant. The rows marked 'COST BASIS: incremental' go to needs-host-cost, as ruled on 2026-10-05. The IETD and Remus rows marked 'COST BASIS: equipment' or 'installed' for the same add-on escape that set-aside (tp-ietd_2013_001-0003, -0005, -0006, -0008 and tp-remus_2013_001-0031: EUR 70 million equipment for a 2 Mt/yr CDQ, JPY 3.5 billion for 450 kt/yr). They become the variant's own capex, 8x below the host, and the cost-ratio rule then carries the error into opex and the levelized cost.
benchmark: Host capex plus a CDQ increment of about 70-200 CAD/t-per-yr, so about 670-800 CAD/t-per-yr
recommendation: Treat 'equipment (of an incremental add-on)' and add-on 'installed' rows as incremental, so they reach needs-host-cost and est-host-increment-capex. Then recompute opex-fixed, opex-variable, and the levelized cost from host plus increment.

value-in-db: total 1.30 t/t, combustion 2.17, process 0.138; ccs variant net 0.30 + captured 1.0
issue: Combustion plus process (2.30 t/t, the Hu 2009 carbon balance, tp-hu_2009_001-0004/-0005) is 1.8x the emissions-total. The total pools Material Economics 2019 1.5 t/t per t steel including casting and hot rolling (tp-material-economics_2019_001-0003), the basis IS013 ruled out for the DRI shaft. It also pools Gielen 1997 1.2-1.3 t/t (tp-gielen_1997_003-0087/-0089), which 'excludes CO in off-gases', so the export gas carbon is missing. The capture variant takes its gross total from this pool, so net plus captured = 1.3 t/t understates the CO2 available for capture.
benchmark: Corex/Finex on-site gross about 2.2-2.9 t CO2/t hot metal before export-gas credit (Hu 2009 Table 4 total 2.30; ETSAP I02 1.57-2.9)
recommendation: Exclude tp-material-economics_2019_001-0003 as for IS013, and set the Gielen rows aside as net of export gas. Rebuild emissions-total from the parts (about 2.3 t/t), then recompute the ccs variant's captured and net values.

issue: The sourced levelized costs are whole-route steel production costs, not the unit's cost. The EAF central is the top-ranked Material Economics 2019 2050 figure (tp-material-economics_2019_001-0015), which includes casting and rolling (EUR 150-200/t) and the metallics, against a calculated 116-159 CAD/t. The electrolytic-hydrogen central is the median of two Material Economics rows on the same downstream basis (-0017, -0021) and Vogl at a 5% interest rate. The electrowinning row (tp-draxler_2021_001-0011) is per t crude steel and includes ore, scrap, alloys, and lime, on an archetype per t reduced iron. Rows like Devlin 2023 include an 8% real discount rate, against the ruling that a sourced levelized cost carries no rate of return.
benchmark: EAF conversion cost about 100-200 CAD/t liquid steel excluding metallics (this database's own lc-calculated-incl-energy 159)
recommendation: Exclude or set aside the total-production-cost rows that include raw materials or downstream rolling (material-economics_2019_001-0015/-0017/-0021, draxler_2021_001-0011, -0003). Keep the remaining route rows on shaft-furnace_electrolytic-hydrogen only after restating them without the rate of return.

issue: The levelized-cost-with-energy step prices the 'heat' target as if it were a carrier, on top of the fuels and steam that already supply that heat. On the cement capture kiln it adds heat 2.9 GJ x 16.76 (lehne-preston_2018_001, copied from the host by ccs-host-plus-addon-energy); on the lime capture kiln heat 6.45 GJ x 16.76 (vattenfall_2018_001); on the absorption chiller heat 1.6 GJ plus its own split natural gas 0.32 and steam 1.28. The hosts kiln_dry-precalciner and kiln_lime-rotary-preheater do not price their heat rows, so host and variant are on different bases. 34 calculated-incl-energy rows across the database carry a heat term.
benchmark: Without the heat term: cement capture kiln about 262 CAD/t, lime capture kiln about 198 CAD/t, absorption chiller about 27.6 CAD/GJ.
recommendation: Price 'heat' only where it is the sole energy row; where named carriers or fuel exist, treat 'heat' as a useful-heat note and leave it out of the energy cost. Better still, stop copying the host's heat row into ccs variants. Re-check all 34 rows.

issue: The captured central is tp-ieaghg_2013_003-0180, 90% capture on a steel-mill lime plant whose own gross is 0.827 t/t. The build nets it off this archetype's host gross of 1.228 t/t, so it records only 61% capture while share-to-capture reads 99.99%. The net total is therefore about four times too high.
benchmark: 90% of the host's 1.228 t/t gross is about 1.105 t/t captured, which leaves a net of about 0.12 t/t.
recommendation: Derive captured CO2 as capture rate x host gross (the way the cement variant comes out at about 93%), or restate each example as a capture rate before pooling. Then re-run emissions-total and abatement cost.

issue: id-zero-combustion-no-fossil set combustion CO2 to zero because the archetype's carriers column lists only steam, yet the archetype holds a natural-gas row of 1.3 GJ/t (judgement guess for the kiln's sintering fuel). The rule's own rationale says it applies only where no energy-use row names a combustible carrier. S94 already flags the carrier list, but not this result.
benchmark: 1.3 GJ/t x about 0.050 t CO2/GJ (ECCC NIR natural gas, HHV) = about 0.065 t/t.
recommendation: Make the zero-combustion rule test the archetype's energy-use rows, not only the carriers column; fix the carriers to electricity; natural-gas (S94); then let id-combustion-co2-from-fuel run.

issue: The archetype has no energy-use row at all. Its only energy example, tp-element-energy_2018_001-0042 (1.05 kWh of electricity per kWh of thermal output), is excluded with 'no conversion from kWh/kWh-thermal-output'. The calculated levelized cost with energy therefore has no energy term, and coverage.csv still marks energy as sourced on the strength of the 95% efficiency row.
benchmark: Useful heat of kiln_tunnel-roller (3.549 GJ/t x 76.6% = 2.72 GJ/t) / 0.95 = about 2.9 GJ/t of electricity; published electric ceramic kilns sit around 2-3.5 GJ/t.
recommendation: Add a rule or judgement: electricity = host useful heat / efficiency, or convert the Element Energy row against kiln_tunnel-roller's useful heat. Make coverage.csv mark energy missing when no energy-use row exists.

issue: The efficient variant uses 36% more energy than its conventional host furnace_regenerative (5.548 GJ/t). The central is Worrell 2008 Table 7 for FLAT glass (tp-worrell_2008_001-0005-total); the other two examples are rehfeldt flat glass (6.61) and a van-geene glass-fibre card TC0066 (11.30). Worrell's container-glass hybrid (natural gas 5.466, tp-worrell_2008_001-0009) gets no total because its electricity twin -0010 is excluded as a repeat. The host pool is mostly container glass. Within Worrell itself the hybrid sits below the regenerative furnace (flat 7.56 against 10.23).
benchmark: Container-glass hybrid about 4.5-6.4 GJ/t, below the host's 5.5 (Worrell container 5.47 + 0.93 = 6.40 against its own regenerative 9.07).
recommendation: Put the furnace family on one product basis (container glass). Let the container example form its total (do not drop -0010, or carry its electricity value into the total), set aside the glass-fibre card TC0066, and add a variant check that an efficient variant's energy use is not above its host's.

issue: The capture add-on steam comes from the ccs.diffuse node median of 2.2 GJ/t CO2 (86% heat), about 1.89 GJ of steam per t CO2. That suits an advanced solvent, not the MEA plants these sources describe. The family's own capture-energy rows in ccs-addon-energy.csv run about twice as high: voldsund_2019_001 MEA 3.07 GJ/t clinker of boiler heat (tp-voldsund_2019_001-0011), ieaghg_2008_001 5.07 GJ/t clinker (-0015), and for lime 2.37-2.39 GJ/t (tp-ieaghg_2013_003-0182, tp-ieaghg_2016_001-0103).
benchmark: MEA reboiler duty of 3.0-3.7 GJ/t CO2 (CEMCAP, IEAGHG 2008) gives about 2.3-2.8 GJ/t clinker and 2.2-2.7 GJ/t lime.
recommendation: Ask Brad whether the capture add-on should represent MEA (the sources) or an advanced solvent. If MEA, use a cement and lime add-on of about 3.3 GJ/t CO2, or take the add-on from ccs-addon-energy.csv where a source isolates it.

value-in-db: BEV 0.0045, FC hydrogen 0.007, trolley 0.008 (diesel 0.0059), dual-fuel 0.0121 GJ/t ore
issue: All four judgement drafts scale from haul-truck_diesel at 0.0117 GJ/t, the value before S89 was fixed (their rationale says so). The diesel host now pools at 0.0226 GJ/t ore, so every sibling sits about 2x low, and the dual-fuel truck now uses about half the energy of the diesel truck it converts, which cannot be.
benchmark: Rescaled with the drafts own ratios on 0.0226: BEV about 0.0080 electricity plus 0.0005 diesel; hydrogen about 0.0136; trolley about 0.0113 diesel plus 0.0040 electricity; dual-fuel about 0.0233 (0.0140 diesel, 0.0093 gas). Diesel fleet 0.016-0.041 GJ/t ore (NRCan 2005, Drebenstedt 2014, Intergroup 2017).
recommendation: Re-draft the four fill-judgement rows from the current host value (or make the drafts ratios to the host so they follow it), and rerun the combustion-CO2 and levelized-cost identities.

archetype: electrolysis-cell_prebaked-anode (and 15 electrolysis-cell archetypes filled from it)
issue: The only sourced value, tp-jrc_2026_001-0004, is EU27 primary output over installed capacity in 2023, which its own note calls low because of the 2022-23 curtailments. Rule est-sibling-capacity-factor copies it to 15 siblings in four families (soderberg, inert-anode, multipolar-chloride, magnesium-chloride, zinc-electrowinning, electrorefining, chlor-alkali cells, and others), which roughly doubles their capital share of levelized cost.
benchmark: Operating aluminium potlines run 95-98 % of the year (IAI; Canadian smelters near full utilization); chlor-alkali and zinc cellhouses 85-95 %.
recommendation: Exclude tp-jrc_2026_001-0004 as a capacity factor (it is a curtailment-year fleet utilization, not a plant factor), or pool it with a normal-year source; re-run est-sibling-capacity-factor so the 15 fills follow.

issue: Where the total has fewer than three examples the build takes the top-ranked single total and then overwrites the carrier as share x total, discarding a much larger carrier pool. SAG-ball: one NRCan gold-mill total (13 kWh/t) replaces ten sourced electricity rows with median 0.072 GJ/t, and nine of the ten lie above the pooled high. Oxy-fuel: one DOE total replaces eleven fuel rows (median 2.46) and the band disappears. Inert-anode: one van-geene card sum (65.6) replaces three electricity rows (median 39.6). This build still shows NM006 (HPGR above SAG) and NM021 (inert anode above prebaked) for this reason.
benchmark: SAG-ball 0.054-0.091 GJ/t ore (Schlesinger 2011, Wang 2013, Norgate 2010); HPGR circuits about 20 % below SAG in the same Wang table; oxy-fuel remelting 2.2-2.9 GJ/t; inert anode 36-55 GJ/t (Martin 2000, Morrey 2002, MPP 2023).
recommendation: Fix the carrier rule (pipeline/carriers.py): when the total pool has n < 3 and a single carrier pool, or the carrier sum, has more examples, take the total from the larger pool and keep the carrier band. Rebuild and recheck NM006 and NM021.

value-in-db: coke 26.892, fuel 26.892, electricity 10.26 GJ/t; combustion CO2 2.96 t/t
issue: The split sets fuel and coke at 100 % of the 26.9 GJ/t total from cusano_2017_001 Table 8.5, because the electricity row (tp-cusano_2017_001-0095, 9.36-11.16) is range-only and pooled apart. The source coke row tp-cusano_2017_001-0096 is 17.5 GJ/t, so coke counts the electricity twice and drives combustion CO2 to 2.96 t/t, 8x the host furnace. The source is also a ferro-chrome furnace per t alloy on a titanium-slag archetype (NM013), so the variant uses twice the energy of its host.
benchmark: Coke 17.5 GJ/t and electricity 9.4-11.2 GJ/t per t ferro-chrome (Cusano 2017 Table 8.5); pre-reduction of ilmenite should cut furnace electricity below the 9.4-9.5 GJ/t host drafts.
recommendation: Let the split use range-only carriers (midpoint) when the split example names them; meanwhile set coke to the 17.5 GJ/t row. Ask Brad whether a ferro-chrome source may stand for titanium slag, or re-draft the variant as a saving on its host.

value-in-db: prebaked process co2e 0.99 [0.38-3.71] with process co2 1.54; soderberg process co2e 3.97 [3.63-8.16]; prebaked total co2e 2.13
issue: Every pooled emissions-process co2e row is PFC only (EPA 2001, NCCP 1999, IAI and MPP notes say so), so process co2e reads lower than process co2. The PFC rows use SAR GWPs (CF4 6500, C2F6 9200) and 1990 emission factors, against the AR5 ruling. The prebaked total co2e 2.13 (tp-mpp_2023_001-0097) includes 0.20 of anode production, which furnace_anode-baking already carries.
benchmark: AR5 process co2e = anode CO2 1.54 + PFC: from the pooled species, CF4 1.5e-4 x 6630 + C2F6 1.5e-5 x 11100 = 1.16, so about 2.7 t/t; current IAI PFC about 0.4-0.9 t CO2e/t Al.
recommendation: Re-target the PFC-only rows to a PFC species or build process co2e from species with AR5 GWPs; drop the 1990-factor NCCP rows or mark them historical; take the anode-production share out of the smelter total.

issue: Both bounds come from tp-gielen_1997_003-0019, whose note says the table sums mining, refining, and smelting and is probably per t aluminium capacity. No basis factor is applied (conversion-factors blank), unlike the gielen and etsap SEC rows fixed under NM002.
benchmark: Divided by cf-alumina-per-aluminium (1.908): about 2,170-4,150 CAD/t-per-yr; greenfield alumina refineries cost about 1,500-3,000 USD per annual t alumina.
recommendation: Add cf-alumina-per-aluminium to the gielen_1997_003 digester_bayer capex example, or exclude it if the row also holds mining and smelting; rerun the cost-ratio fills that follow from it.

issue: The range-midpoint pools two crundwell_2011_001 rows on different bases: tp-crundwell_2011_001-0044 per annual t Ni+Co (19,703-23,644) and tp-crundwell_2011_001-0046 per annual t concentrate feed (236-284). The midpoint fits neither, and the 100x band flows to opex and levelized cost.

recommendation: Exclude tp-crundwell_2011_001-0046 (per t feed) on this per-t-metal archetype; rebuild.

issue: The only example, tp-aries_2024_001-0055, is the refractory lining lifetime, and its note says so ("not the furnace"). A 6-year plant life more than doubles the capital share of levelized cost and sits far below the 25 years of melting-furnace_reverberatory-rotary.

recommendation: Exclude tp-aries_2024_001-0055 as a plant lifetime (or re-target it to a component lifetime); let the class or sibling rule fill about 25 years.

issue: The high, tp-etsap_2012_001-0015, is per t aluminium (its note says so) and takes no cf-anode-per-aluminium factor, while the doe_2017_001 rows do. issue: tp-cusano_2017_001-x004 restates the printed 25.2-32.4 GJ/t of refinery heat as 25 % net purchased heat, which contradicts the gross-input ruling. value-in-db: no row at all (feedstock-consumption = 1 GJ/GJ identity)

recommendation: Add an identity rule (or extend id-feedstock-in-product) that writes specific-energy-consumption = feed per product - product energy, from the sourced efficiency, with the feed carrier as target.

issue: A fluid coker burns about a quarter of its coke in the burner vessel to heat the reactor, but the carriers name only electricity and steam (doe_1998_001 Table 4-6, which prints no fired fuel row), so the zero-combustion identity fires. The 0.68 GJ/m3 electricity also comes from the one DOE row (tp-doe_1998_001-0031, 30 kWh/bbl) while the two Meyers 1997 rows on the same pool (tp-meyers_1997_001-0097, -0100) give 0.5 kWh/bbl excluding the air blower; the central is the DOE row, not the median.

recommendation: Add petroleum-coke as a carrier (energy use, ruling 4) with a sourced or drafted coke-burn value, let id-combustion-co2 or a judgement write the CO2, and re-check why the DOE electricity row sets the central over the Meyers rows.

value-in-db: 6e-06 GJ/m3; annual-output 1.7e9 m3; capex 0.02 CAD per m3/yr
issue: The drafts are per m3-km (the rationale says so and asks for a re-read) but the unit columns say m3, so annual-output 1.7e9 'm3' is really m3-km and the archetype is not comparable with its siblings. The draft also takes 0.05 bar/km, a low-velocity light-crude gradient; Canadian dilbit lines run 0.2-0.5 bar/km.

recommendation: Settle the product unit (m3-km) in archetype.csv and the unit strings, then redraft the SEC near 1e-4 GJ/m3-km with a cited gradient or a sourced pipeline power figure.

issue: The tier-1 add-on is etsap_2014_001 'with capture 3800 less without 2000' per m3/yr, which makes capture cost more than the whole upgrader. Already open as S100; this build still shows it.

recommendation: Resolve S100: drop the ETSAP difference and use the tier-2 capture-node cost x 0.068 t/m3, or Quest as a same-source add-on.

issue: Both carriers come from Suhr 2015 p.81 Sect. 2.5.2, which gives 6000 kWh/t heat and 2500 kWh/t power for a whole non-integrated TAD tissue mill, not for the through-air dryer. The whole-mill figure then drives a guessed natural-gas split of 17.28 GJ/t, combustion CO2 of 0.875 t/t and a levelized cost with energy of 1090 $/t.

recommendation: Mark the two Suhr p.81 rows whole-plant and exclude them from the dryer; re-read Suhr Table 7.18 (the sc-013 row, now blank) for a dryer-only value.

value-in-db: steam 2.031 GJ/t = total; no electricity row
issue: The total of 2.031 GJ/t comes from UKERC (ct_2011_001) press-section savings applied to the base, and id-single-carrier-split then puts the whole total on steam. The host paper-machine has electricity 1.234 and steam 1.125 GJ/t, so the strong variant shows steam up 80 % and electricity gone.

recommendation: Split the variant's total with the host's carrier shares (est-variant-host-split, as paper-machine_efficiency-moderate does) instead of id-single-carrier-split; fix the rule so it does not fire when the host has more than one carrier.

issue: DEA 2026 sheet 89 (tp-dea_2026_003-0224) gives the feed as biomass-solid, but records/reference/feedstock.csv lists this archetype's feedstock only as 'biomass', so the feed was never taken off. The archetype also carries the identity feedstock-consumption of 1 GJ/GJ, so the feed is counted twice.
benchmark: After take-off: about 0.16 GJ/GJ biomass plus 0.058 electricity (about 0.22 GJ/GJ total).
recommendation: Change the feedstock.csv row to 'biomass|biomass-solid|fuel' (as fermenter_lignocellulosic-enzymatic has); check every biofuels row in feedstock.csv against the carriers its examples use.

issue: DEA 2026 sheet 105 (tp-dea_2026_003-0401) counts the grain feed as 1.716 GJ/GJ biomass-solid. The archetype is not in feedstock.csv, so the grain stays in SEC, sets the 2.08 high, and its 84/16 share then splits fuel into biomass-solid 0.28 and natural gas 0.054. All seven Mueller 2013 and Kwiatkowski 2006 natural-gas rows give 0.16-0.34 GJ/GJ, and US dry mills burn gas, not biomass. Variants _efficiency-moderate and _ccs-concentrated copy the split.
benchmark: Natural gas 0.23-0.34 GJ/GJ (Mueller and Kwik 2013, 19,500-26,200 Btu/gal), biomass about 0; electricity 0.023-0.030.
recommendation: Add fermenter_grain-dry-mill* to feedstock.csv (biomass|biomass-solid, product-energy 1) so the DEA grain comes off; then pick the fuel split from a natural-gas source, not from DEA.

issue: id-zero-combustion-no-fossil fires because the variant's own carrier list is electricity and steam, yet the fermenter variant carries natural gas 0.049 GJ/GJ in its SEC (host 0.0027 t/GJ) and the dryer variant's host and strong sibling carry 0.150 and 0.139 t/t. A moderate measure shows a 100 % cut in combustion CO2.

recommendation: Make the zero-combustion identity read the carriers in the variant's own SEC rows (and its host's), not the archetype carrier list; else use est-variant-host-combustion as the strong dryer does.

issue: var-host-capacity and host-size copy the biofuels anaerobic-digester (a biogas plant on a GJ basis) onto a pulp-mill effluent digester whose product is m3 of effluent. The capacity is in MW and the annual output of 934,563 is GJ of biogas but now reads as m3 of effluent.

recommendation: For a capture or efficiency variant, take the host's efficiency (less any capture penalty) ahead of the sibling tiers.

issue: Both pooled rows are Geleynse 2018 Table 2 mass yields, and the notes say 'MASS yield ... not an energy efficiency'. The Tao 2017 rows (0.95 GGE fuel per GGE ethanol) drop out because no heating-value stream exists for this archetype.

recommendation: Exclude the Geleynse mass-yield rows from efficiency (record them as a yield, if anywhere); add a heating-value-stream entry for reactor_alcohol-to-jet so the Tao rows convert.

issue: Two rows break the band. The low of 0.817 is the build's carrier total for Suhr 2015 Table 3.29, which holds only sootblowing steam and electricity, so it lacks the liquor. recommendation: Do not form an example total from carriers that omit the fired fuel; restate or exclude the Martin per-product row; close S79 with a per-ADt to per-t-BLS factor.

issue: Still present from OT016. The total is top-ranked tp-cusano_2017_001-0039, whose note says 'energy use for the overall plant (sum of treatment, smelting and holding)', and the electricity carrier takes 100% of it, though its own 18 rows (Kermeli 2016, NCCP 1999, Aries 2024) cluster at 1.3-3.0 GJ/t. The SEC also disagrees with the archetype's 79.5% efficiency.
benchmark: Coreless induction melting of iron 520-650 kWh/t = 1.9-2.3 GJ/t (Aries 2024 Table 2.25; NCCP 1999 480 kWh/t)
recommendation: Exclude or set aside tp-cusano_2017_001-0039 as whole-plant scope and let the electricity median (about 1.8-2.0 GJ/t) set the total.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
archetype: mobile-equipment_diesel; mobile-equipment_battery-electric; mobile-equipment_diesel-electric; mobile-equipment_spark-ignition; mobile-equipment_hydrogen-fuel-cell; mobile-equipment_hydrogen-combustion
issue: Mobile equipment has no class pool, so the rule takes the median of all 102 archetypes, which are mostly continuous process plant. The family's own annual-output guess assumes 1,500-2,000 h/yr at half load, about 10-20% of nameplate. At 90% the capex share of every levelized cost in the family is 4.5-9 times too low.
benchmark: Forklifts, loaders, and mine mobile fleet 1,500-5,000 h/yr, 10-35% capacity factor on a nameplate-power basis
recommendation: Give mobile-equipment its own capacity-factor guess (about 20%, band 10-35%) or a class pool; stop the class-all fallback for families with duty-cycle equipment.

family: petroleum-refining; other-industry; machine-drive; space-conditioning; mobile-equipment; lighting
issue: The central 100% is 'derived from 1 example' (tp-ieaghg_2017_002-0235, a per-source design table) and overrides five sourced plant-level rates of 90-90.2% (IEAGHG 2017, NREL 2018, Collodi 2010). Captured then exceeds the host gross total (0.0567), and the net total clips to zero. Same pattern as MC013 in cement and the 99.77% on steam-reformer_methane_ccs-concentrated.
benchmark: Flue-gas MEA capture on an SMR 89-90%; net about 0.008 t/GJ H2 (10% of host gross)
recommendation: Pool share-to-capture as the median of the printed plant-level rates and use a derived captured/emitted ratio only where no printed rate exists; recompute captured and net total.

issue: Several feed-inclusive rows escape the take-off because they are tagged 'fuel': martin_2000_001 Chemicals-7 fuel 33.8 MBtu/short-ton (39.3 GJ/t), ietd_2013_001 fuel 36.9 GJ/t (40.9 HHV, the page calls it total energy), and rouwenhorst_2019_001 naphtha reformer 9.7 kWh/kg (38.7 GJ/t, also a naphtha route on a gas archetype). They set the band's high and pull the central up.
benchmark: After the feed is off, SMR fuel and steam-raising is about 7-12 GJ/t HHV (JRC 2007 Table 2.6: 29-36 GJ/t total LHV less 22.5 feed).
recommendation: Same fix as CHEM003 (test 'fuel' rows on reformers against the threshold), and exclude or re-map the Rouwenhorst naphtha-reformer row.

issue: Van Geene 2024 card TC0078 (27.6 GJ/t, mostly hydrogen) is first multiplied in full by the hydrogen HHV/LHV factor (1.18), then the 25.2 GJ/t stoichiometric hydrogen is taken off. What is left (7.4) mixes the hydrogen HHV gap with the card's other inputs. This explains open item S128.
benchmark: Armijo and Philibert 2020: 0.9 MWh/t (3.24 GJ/t) for loop, ASU and H2 compression; DEA 2026: 1.2 GJ/t electricity.
recommendation: Take the hydrogen off on the source's own basis before the heating-value factor, or apply the factor only to the hydrogen part; failing that, rule the MIDDEN total out and use the carrier sum (about 3.2 GJ/t).

issue: The capex pool holds boulamanti_2017_001 p.110 'typical cost of membranes per t Cl2' (EUR 20/t, read as 43.5 CAD per t of annual capacity). That is a membrane replacement cost, an operating consumable, not plant capex, and it sets the band's low at a fiftieth of the central.
benchmark: Greenfield membrane plants cost about EUR 1000 per t/yr Cl2 (Brinkmann 2014; Boulamanti 2017), 2100-2400 CAD/t-per-yr.
recommendation: Exclude the membrane-cost row from capex (or move it to opex-variable as a consumable); the band then runs about 2100-2400.

value-in-db: opex-fixed 279.8 CAD/t-per-yr; opex-variable 251.8 CAD/t (both Gielen 1997, n=1)
issue: Fixed O&M rests on an assumed correction (sc-006) that reads Gielen 1997 Table 2.5.3's printed 10 ECU/t-yr as 100, which makes fixed O&M 13% of capex a year; variable O&M is Gielen's 90 ECU/t including labour. Together they give about 530 CAD/t of non-energy O&M, 12-14x the family medians, and screen-backtest shows the cost-ratio rule would give 64 and 44.
benchmark: Non-energy O&M for chlor-alkali is typically 3-5% of capex a year (about 65-110 CAD/t-per-yr) plus salt and chemicals.
recommendation: Revisit sc-006 (the printed 10 ECU may be right) and check whether Gielen's variable O&M includes electricity or salt; ask Brad which reading to keep.

issue: The joosten_1998_001 MTO rows (Tables 18-19: fuel 12.3, steam 1.1, electricity 0.3 GJ) are per t ethylene, but they pool on this per-t-HVC archetype with only a heating-value factor; the 2026-10-13 fix (CH001, CH013) added t HVC per t ethylene factors for crackers and biomass routes only. The natural-gas guess then names that fuel as gas, although the MTO reaction is exothermic and Joosten's fuel is the process's own fuel gas.
benchmark: IEA 2018: 11 GJ per t HVC net process energy; an MTO unit makes roughly 1 t propylene per t ethylene, so per-t-ethylene figures are about 2x the per-t-HVC ones.
recommendation: Add a cf-hvc-per-ethylene factor for Joosten's MTO case and rebuild; re-check whether the fuel carrier should be process off-gas rather than natural gas.

value-in-db: opex-variable 3655 CAD/t (3478-3812); no SEC and no feedstock-consumption row
issue: Still as in CH021 (2026-10-11, left as a note). The four mantei_2021_001 Table 7 rows are 'raw materials and utilities' and their notes state they include hydrogen at 4241 EUR/t and CO2 at 309 EUR/t. The archetype still has no SEC or hydrogen feedstock row, so the model can price neither energy nor feed except through this opex.
benchmark: Non-feed variable O&M for e-fuel synthesis is typically 2-5% of capex a year (about 60-150 CAD/t); hydrogen about 0.4-0.5 t per t OME.
recommendation: Strip hydrogen and CO2 out of the Mantei opex (or set it aside), and add feedstock-consumption hydrogen from stoichiometry plus an electricity and steam SEC.

value-in-db: 3.47 CAD/t-CO2-eq on co2-to-methanol (n=1) and as the low of haber-bosch-electrolytic (208.6, 3.47-415); reduction potential 9% on co2-to-methanol
issue: Both come from IPCC AR6 WGIII Table 11.3 rows that print exactly 2.0 USD/t-CO2-eq. The row mapped to reactor_co2-to-methanol is 'catalysis of olefins from (m)ethanol, H2 and COx', an olefins route, not CO2 to methanol. An identical 2.0 on both options looks like a category entry rather than a cost.
benchmark: Electrolytic ammonia abatement costs 100-500 CAD/t-CO2 (Material Economics 2019: EUR 108-215); e-methanol is of the same order.
recommendation: Re-read the Table 11.3 cost column; if 2.0 is a category, exclude both rows. Re-map the olefins row to reactor_methanol-to-olefins.

value-in-db: 10.18 GJ/t, labelled electricity (total 10.18 from van-geene TC0484)
issue: The split takes Singh 2021 (electricity only, 1756 kWh/t = 6.32 GJ/t) as a 100% share of the MIDDEN total, so the whole 10.18 GJ/t becomes electricity, though Singh's own figure is 6.32 and the archetype lists steam as its carrier.
benchmark: Singh 2021 SI Table S4: 6.32 GJ/t electricity; the remaining 3.9 GJ/t is most likely steam or heat.
recommendation: Same fix as CHEM002: no 100% share from a single-carrier example; keep electricity at 6.32 and leave the rest unassigned or as steam.

issue: Still as in CH019 (2026-10-11, left as a note): the median of four IEA 2013 values sits below the 1.6 GJ/t endothermic heat of ethanol dehydration, and the archetype still lists no carriers and no ethanol feed.
benchmark: About 2 GJ/t (DECHEMA via IEA 2013) or more with separation; ethanol feed about 1.7 t per t ethylene.
recommendation: Take the 2 GJ/t value as central, give the archetype carriers (steam or natural gas), and add the ethanol feedstock-consumption.

issue: Still as in CH022 (2026-10-11, left as a note): one IEA 2018 row sets capex at 7.9x the family median, and the fixed O&M fills from it; the source scope has not been re-read.
benchmark: Biomass-gasification ammonia is roughly 2-3x an SMR plant, about 2500-4000 CAD/t-per-yr.
recommendation: Re-read iea_2018_001 for scope (first-of-a-kind, feedstock handling, or per t of a different product) and widen or lower the central.

value-in-db: emissions-total co2e -0.0482432 t/GJ; emissions-combustion co2 central 0 (low 0, high 0.16)
issue: The negative co2e is UKERC CH-MC1 'Specific emissions' (tp-aea_2010_001-0008), a saving against a baseline, not an emission. The CO2 central is the AEA hydrogen fuel cell (0), while the archetype's only SEC carrier is natural gas at 3.17 GJ/GJ, so the emissions and the energy describe different machines.
benchmark: Natural-gas SOFC CHP: about 3.17 x 0.0503 = 0.16 t CO2 per GJ heat (IEAGHG 2007, tp-ieaghg_2007_001-0168).
recommendation: Exclude the UKERC co2e row. Make the CO2 central consistent with the SEC carrier (natural gas), or split hydrogen and natural-gas fuel cells.

issue: The co2e central sits below the CO2 central, which is impossible. The co2e pool is five JRC 2014 rows per GWh with 'electricity assumed' (tp-jrc_2014_001-0363 to -0407) on an archetype whose product is heat, while the CO2 row is IEAGHG 2007 per MWth of heat.
benchmark: co2e at or above CO2: about 0.097-0.10 t per GJ of heat for a gas turbine CHP.
recommendation: Put the JRC rows on a per-GJ-heat basis with the source's heat-to-power ratio, or exclude them; let co2e come from the identity.

value-in-db: co2e 0.266528 t/GJ (JRC biomass plants); co2 0.0885603; emissions-total co2 0.275
issue: The co2e central comes from JRC 2014 biomass grate and fluidised-bed plants (tp-jrc_2014_001-0156 to -0218), so biogenic CO2 sits in a fossil parameter, against the emissions-biomass ruling. The archetype's SEC carrier is steam (3.56 GJ/GJ), so boiler combustion is outside its scope anyway, and the CO2 row is the coal fuel factor from HPCH001.
benchmark: A turbine fed with steam has no combustion emissions; if the archetype is meant to be the whole plant, coal is about 0.22 t/GJ electricity and biomass belongs in emissions-biomass.
recommendation: Decide the scope (turbine only vs whole plant, ask Brad). Move the JRC biomass rows to emissions-biomass, and fix the EIA row through HPCH001.

issue: The tier-1 add-on is Weidmann 2013 VAROM 7.2 Rp/kWh electricity (tp-weidmann_2013_001-0060 and -0069), which the record marks as the whole plant including capture. The build treats it as the capture add-on and adds it to the host, so it counts the plant's own O&M twice, and the add-on disagrees with tier 2 by 29x.
benchmark: Capture variable O&M about 5-15 CAD/t CO2 x 0.084 t/GJ = 0.4-1.3 CAD per GJ heat; whole plant about 4-5 CAD/GJ.
recommendation: Treat 'INCLUDES CAPTURE' rows as whole-plant values (subtract the same-source host, or use them as the variant's own cost), else fall back to tier 2. Check the capex add-on the same way (tier 1 89.7 vs tier 2 34.1). Related to S68 and S103.

value-in-db: combined-cycle_ccs 50.4686 % vs host 49.1337 %; CHP ccs electric 46.9318 % vs host 37.2905 %
issue: Both capture variants come out more efficient than their hosts. The central on combined-cycle_ccs-diffuse is the median of Irlam 45.7%, and Weidmann 2013 MARKAL 56% and 61% LHV (tp-weidmann_2013_001-0049, -0055); 61% LHV with capture is beyond any built or designed NGCC with CCS. The variant's own SEC of 2.22 implies 45%.
benchmark: NGCC with 90-95% capture: 45-47% HHV (Irlam 2017 45.7%, EIA 2024 47.1%), about 7 points below the host.
recommendation: Check whether the Weidmann rows are capture cases. If they are not, re-map them; if they are, exclude them as outliers. Prefer Irlam and EIA for the central.

value-in-db: emissions-total -0.835 t/t (low -1, high -0.468); electricity 0.4932 GJ/t with n=29 but no band
issue: The negative emissions-total and the 1.878 GJ/t total come from MIDDEN whole capture-system cards (van-geene_2024_001 tc0017 post-combustion CCS system, tc0481 and tc0483 incinerator add-ons, tc0540) mapped onto the compressor; compression does not capture CO2. The electricity central is the split example (DEA 2024 biogas CO2 liquefaction, tp-dea_2024_002-0065) and not the median of 29, though liquefaction is a different service. The total is already S123.
benchmark: Compression and drying to pipeline pressure: 0.23-0.36 GJ/t (IEAGHG 2016 and 2017 rows); emissions-total about 0.
recommendation: Re-map the MIDDEN capture-system cards to capture-unit_amine (or the capture family's matching archetype). Pool the electricity carrier as a median when the split example is a different service.

issue: The DEA 2026 wood-chip heat-only boilers with flue-gas condensation print 114-115% on LHV (tp-dea_2026_006-0322, -0332, -0342). The generic cf-hhv-lhv-solid-liquid factor (about 0.95) leaves them at 108-109% on HHV, which is above 100%.
benchmark: For wet wood chips (about 45% moisture) the as-received LHV/HHV ratio is about 0.80, giving about 91-92% HHV.
recommendation: Add a wood-chip (moist biomass) HHV/LHV factor to the heating-value stream table for these DEA rows, or cap HHV efficiency at 100% in the bounds check.

issue: The note says H2A counts all feedstock carbon converted to CO2 on site; for a biomass gasifier that is biogenic CO2, which the ruling puts in emissions-biomass, not in the fossil emissions-total.
benchmark: Fossil CO2 near zero (auxiliary natural gas 0.045 GJ/GJ x 0.05 = 0.002 t/GJ); about 0.18 t/GJ biogenic.
recommendation: Move the row to emissions-biomass and let fossil emissions-total come from the fossil carriers.

issue: est-host-increment-capex adds the increment from one UKERC measure, 'CHP for mercury cell process chlorine' (ukerc_2013_001:combined-cycle_efficiency-moderate@chp-for-mercury-cell-process-chlorine), which is a chlor-alkali CHP project, not a combined-cycle efficiency upgrade.
benchmark: An efficiency-moderate CCGT should cost about the same as the host, or up to 10-20% more.
recommendation: Re-map or exclude that UKERC example; fill capex from the host with a small increment, or leave it unfilled.

issue: The unabated ATR emits less per GJ of hydrogen than its own capture variant captures (0.0622 t/GJ). On HHV, 0.049 t/GJ is about 7 kg CO2 per kg H2.
benchmark: Unabated ATR with fired heater: about 9-10 kg CO2/kg H2, or 0.063-0.070 t/GJ HHV.
recommendation: Check the MIDDEN row's basis (LHV, partial capture, or feedstock-only), and prefer a whole-plant source; this feeds HPCH003.

issue: The same unit converts on one row and not on its siblings. tp-rechberger_2020_001-0013 (635 m3/t H2) converts through cf-h2-hhv-volume, but tp-rechberger_2020_001-0011 (800 m3/t H2) is excluded with 'no conversion from m3/t to GJ/t'. So are the natural-gas rows -0005 (48 m3/t) and -0012 (50 m3/t), which are the only direct evidence for the small gas carrier on this route.
benchmark: 800 m3 x 12.75 MJ/m3 HHV = 10.2 GJ/t H2; 50 m3 NG x about 39 MJ/m3 HHV = about 1.9 GJ/t
recommendation: Find why the factor applies to -0013 only (a per-example heating-value stream row?). Apply cf-h2-hhv-volume to every H2 m3/t row, and add or apply a natural-gas volume HHV factor so the -0005 and -0012 rows convert.

issue: The combustion CO2 exceeds the total it belongs to. The total is a single model result, Rechberger 2020 0.453 t/t for the 'DR core process' (tp-rechberger_2020_001-0002), while the ETSAP I02 combustion rows give 0.53-0.65 t/t. The pooled natural gas of 11.3 GJ/t at about 0.050 t CO2/GJ HHV gives 0.57 t/t. The ccs variant inherits the low total (net 0.203 + captured 0.25).
benchmark: Gas-based MIDREX/Energiron about 0.5-0.65 t CO2/t DRI direct
recommendation: Let id-total-from-parts or a check flag an emissions-total below its own combustion row. Either add the ETSAP rows to the total pool or take the total from the parts, then recompute the ccs variant.

issue: The central is the hydrogen-fired case of Siyambalapitiya 2026 at USD 3/kg H2 (tp-siyambalapitiya_2026_001-0013). The only other row (-0007, 43.3) is the gas case and includes a USD 60/t CO2 carbon price. The archetype's carriers are oil and natural gas, and its calculated cost including energy is 24.6 CAD/t. The 2026-09-29 decision pools hydrogen billet reheating here, but the central should not then be the hydrogen case.
benchmark: Gas-fired reheating about 15-35 CAD/t (calculated-incl-energy 24.6; Siyambalapitiya gas case without the carbon price)
recommendation: Set aside -0013 for the cost (it prices a different fuel), and restate -0007 without the carbon price, or ask Brad whether the hydrogen cost rows belong on furnace_reheating at all.

issue: The efficient variant is 25 points below its host. The rows are JRC 2022 Table 2.23 'heat to steel / fuel SEC' derivations (tp-jrc_2022_001-0062, -0064). As the fuel SEC falls with hot charging (1.25 and 0.94 GJ/t), the heat needed by the steel falls faster, so the ratio drops. They measure charge temperature, not furnace efficiency. The host's 61% includes the hydrogen-furnace row of Siyambalapitiya (62%).
benchmark: Recuperative or regenerative furnaces about 60-75% (Stork 2014 75% best new)
recommendation: Set aside the JRC Table 2.23 derived efficiencies on hot-charged cases, or define efficiency for cold charge only. Leave the variant's efficiency empty or take Stork 2014.

value-in-db: BF eff-strong 1.204 t/t against host 1.099; coke eff-strong 0.784 against host 0.775
issue: Efficient variants emit more than their hosts. Each variant total is Pardo 2013's own base minus Pardo's BAT change (tp-pardo_2013_001-0064: 1.219-0.015; -0052: 0.794-0.010). The host central comes from a different source (Otto 2017 1.099 for the blast furnace), so the absolute values do not compare.
benchmark: Host central x (1 - Pardo's relative change): BF about 1.085, coke about 0.765 t/t
recommendation: Derive these as a relative change applied to the host's pooled central, as ukercsaving does for SEC (fix the ordering first, see IS001), or drop the variant total and let the variant combustion rule fill it.

issue: The three UKERC 'Specific emissions' rows (tp-ukerc_2013_001-0011, -0016, -0021; DC furnace, twin-shell shaft, Comelt) are 2-3x the host's direct total, and about equal to direct CO2 plus grid electricity at about 400 kWh/t. So they most likely include indirect electricity CO2, the defect already ruled out for Energetics 2000 (tp-doe_2000_001-0005 etc.). A scrap-preheating variant should not emit more than its host on scope 1.
benchmark: EAF direct (scope 1) 0.08-0.15 t CO2/t (Pardo 2013 0.14, host 0.11)
recommendation: Check UKERC's definition of 'Specific emissions' for the IS-EAF rows. If it includes electricity, set these aside as scope 2 inclusive.

issue: The EAF value is ETSAP I02 'O&M costs are about $32/t-yr' (tp-etsap_2010_002-0040), a per-annual-tonne (fixed) figure loaded as variable cost. It is 6x the scrap-preheating variant's 13.3 and fails the backtest (ratio 0.048). On smelting reduction, the de Beer 1998 rows (tp-de-beer_1998_001-0008 etc.) are 'variable cost per t hot metal (raw materials, labour, energy, maintenance, less gas credits)'. They count energy already in SEC and ore and coal, which sets the 398 high. Hismelt 18.55 USD/t-yr (-0028) has the same per-t-yr issue.
benchmark: EAF non-energy variable O&M (electrodes, refractories, oxygen) about 20-40 CAD/t
recommendation: Re-read the ETSAP per-t-yr O&M rows as opex-fixed. Exclude the de Beer variable-cost rows from opex-variable, because they include energy and raw materials.

issue: The fuel split comes from one Dutch integrated-works pellet plant (Remus 2013 Table 4.1 note 3, tp-remus_2013_001-0013 to -0017), which fires coke breeze and COG/BOF gas. The archetype's carriers are natural gas, electricity, and coal, and its note says most Canadian pelletizing is at the mines (IOC, AM Mining Canada, Tilden-type straight grates), where natural gas or oil is the fuel. Gielen 1997 and Daniels 2002 both give the fuel as gas.
benchmark: Mine-site straight-grate or grate-kiln: fuel mostly natural gas or HFO, about 0.4-0.6 GJ/t, plus electricity about 0.15-0.2 GJ/t
recommendation: Take the fuel split from a gas-fired example (Gielen 1997, Daniels 2002) rather than the integrated-works plant, or ask Brad which plant type the archetype represents.

issue: The pool mixes whole-plant electricity with the host's kiln-only figure. voldsund_2019_001 (tp-voldsund_2019_001-0018) is gross power for the cement plant plus capture; agora_2021_001 (-0111) is per t cement, including the whole plant; ieaghg_2008_001 gives both kiln-only 0.30 (-0058) and whole-plant 0.69 (-0078). The host kiln_dry-precalciner carries kiln-only 0.095 GJ/t, so the oxy-fuel kiln shows an increase of about 285 kWh/t. Calcium looping takes the same Voldsund whole-plant basis.
benchmark: CSI-ECRA 2017 TP 43 (tp-csi-ecra_2017_001-0123): an increase of 117-180 kWh/t clinker over a 70 kWh/t reference. That gives kiln-only about 0.5-0.75 GJ/t.
recommendation: Set aside the whole-plant rows (Voldsund gross, Agora, IEAGHG whole-plant) or rebase them to the kiln with a plant-electricity split. Keep the CSI-ECRA increase plus the host's kiln electricity.

value-in-db: electricity 0.248 GJ/t; coal 1.209, natural gas 0.537, petroleum coke 0.940 (guesses)
issue: The electricity is Worrell 2022 best-practice WHOLE-PLANT electricity (62 kWh/t cement, rebased to 68.9 kWh/t clinker, tp-worrell_2022_001-x001), against the host's kiln-only 0.095 GJ/t. The efficient variant therefore shows 2.6 times its host's electricity. Its fuel split is a fresh guess with 34% petroleum coke, while the host and the moderate variant use the host's PCA mix (4% petroleum coke).
benchmark: Kiln-only best practice is about 20-25 kWh/t clinker (0.07-0.09 GJ/t). The fuel split should follow the host (coal 55%, natural gas 37%, oil 4%, petroleum coke 4%), as the moderate variant does with est-variant-host-split.
recommendation: Exclude or rescope tp-worrell_2022_001-x001 for the kiln. Drop the three judgement fuel guesses so est-variant-host-split runs as it does on the moderate variant.

issue: Both variants take est-cost-ratio-opex-variable (0.065 x their capex), which gives more than twice the host kiln_dry-precalciner's sourced 14.71 CAD/t. Their capex and opex-fixed come from the host by est-host-increment, so only the variable O&M breaks the host-plus-increment pattern. That pushes the strong variant's calculated levelized cost (126.2) above the host's (111.1).
benchmark: About the host's 14.7 CAD/t; efficiency measures do not double non-energy variable O&M.
recommendation: Run est-host-increment for opex-variable on variants that have a host, or copy the host's value, before the cost-ratio rule.

issue: Both values come from one steel-mill-integrated lime plant in ieaghg_2013_003 (tp-ieaghg_2013_003-0132 and -0130). The total sits below the archetype's own process 0.785 plus combustion 0.3135 (1.10 t/t). The only named fuel is coke-oven gas, which the archetype's carriers (natural gas, coal, coke) do not list and which a merchant lime plant does not have. The pooled total energy use (4.05 GJ/t) is also set by that plant.
benchmark: Merchant shaft and PFR kilns emit about 1.0-1.2 t CO2/t lime (EuLA in Schorcht 2013; Simoni 2022: 1.0-1.8 including fuel) and burn natural gas, coal, or coke.
recommendation: Set aside the IEAGHG steel-mill lime rows for this archetype (or route them to an iron-and-steel lime plant), let id-total-from-parts set the total, and give the fuel split from the merchant sources.

value-in-db: total 0.263 t/t (low 0.215, high 1.3); ccs variant net 0.050, captured 0.213
issue: Still below the archetype's own combustion 0.23 plus process 0.18 (0.41) after the MC015 fix. The two remaining van-geene cards (TC0001 0.263, TC0002 0.215) are electrically boosted, high-cullet furnaces, and wsp_2015_003 (0.334) does not say what it covers. The capture variant inherits the low total, so its captured CO2 and net total both come out low.
benchmark: An air-fuel container furnace at 5.4 GJ/t natural gas (about 0.27 t/t) plus 0.1-0.18 t/t carbonate CO2 gives about 0.37-0.45 t/t.
recommendation: Let id-total-from-parts set the total where the pooled total falls below combustion plus process. Otherwise set aside the boosted high-cullet cards. Re-derive the capture variant.

value-in-db: electric: total 0.0394, process 0.21, reduction 100%; oxy-fuel: total 0.20 (low 0.03), no process row
issue: The electric melter's total is van-geene TC0011 (process only, high cullet, tp-van-geene_2024_001-0053), but its process row is Gielen 1997 at 100% primary batch (tp-gielen_1997_001-0292). The total is therefore five times below the process CO2 alone, and the 100% reduction (wsp_2015_003-0004) cannot hold while carbonate CO2 remains. The oxy-fuel pool still holds fuel-switched cards, the same defect as MC015: green-gas TC0008 (0.0394), green-gas glass fibre TC0067 (0.03), and hydrogen glass wool TC0072 (0.159), which set the low at 0.03.
benchmark: Put both on one cullet basis: carbonate CO2 0.05-0.2 t/t. The electric melter's reduction against the regenerative host is then about 50-90%, not 100%.
recommendation: Put process and total on one cullet assumption, or let id-total-from-parts decide. Set aside TC0008, TC0067, and TC0072 from furnace_oxy-fuel as was done for TC0003. Replace or cap the 100% reduction.

issue: id-combustion-co2-from-fuel skips an archetype whenever a process-CO2 row exists, even a zero one, and wherever only an unnamed fuel is known (design.md). kiln_legacy has named fuels (coal 3.22, petroleum coke 1.00, natural gas 0.12, oil 0.04 GJ/t) and process 0.506, but no combustion row. binder_carbonated has natural gas 2.6 GJ/t and process 0, but no combustion row. The direct-fired dryer has only a total.
benchmark: kiln_legacy about 0.40-0.45 t/t (fuels x NIR factors; also its total 0.96 less process 0.506); binder_carbonated about 0.13 t/t; dryer_rotary-direct-fired about 0.0125 t/t (equal to its total).
recommendation: Let the rule run alongside a process row (it computes only the combustion part). For a single-fuel or unnamed-fuel archetype, set combustion = total - process where both exist.

issue: The combustion value is the midpoint of the Schorcht 2013 EuLA range (tp-schorcht_2013_001-0040, est-range-midpoint). On the archetype's fuel of 6.214 GJ/t it implies 0.115 t CO2/GJ, more than coal emits. The archetype's own fuel split (coal and natural gas 40% each, petroleum coke 20%) gives far less, and the total inherits the excess.
benchmark: 6.214 GJ/t at about 0.077 t/GJ (the split's weighted NIR factor) = about 0.48 t/t combustion; total about 1.26 t/t.
recommendation: Prefer id-combustion-co2-from-fuel over a range midpoint when the midpoint implies an emission factor above every listed fuel's, or check the midpoint against the fuel split. Then re-run id-total-from-parts.

value-in-db: efficiency 120% (low 68); energy use 1.6 GJ heat per GJ cooling
issue: The two describe different machines. The efficiency central is a direct-fired double-effect chiller (tp-eia_2023_002-0055, COP 1.2), while the energy use is the typical single-effect figure (kermeli_2011_001, stuckrath_2022_001, COP 0.625). 1.6 GJ/GJ implies an efficiency of 62.5%, not 120%. HP021 (2026-10-11) accepted a 71.5% central that this build no longer has.
benchmark: Single-effect LiBr chiller: COP 0.65-0.75 (efficiency about 70%, energy use about 1.4 GJ/GJ). Double-effect: COP 1.0-1.2.
recommendation: Pick one machine for the archetype (single-effect steam-fired fits food-plant waste-heat use). Then set aside the EIA direct-fired row or move it to a gas-fired variant, so that efficiency and energy use agree.

value-in-db: capacity factor 10% (guess); calculated levelized cost 12.25 CAD/GJ against 2.43 for chiller_high-efficiency
issue: A 2026-10-21 judgement draft gives the conventional chiller a 10% capacity factor (HVAC hours), while its siblings take the 60% class median. The conventional machine therefore costs five times more per GJ of cooling than the efficient one, despite a lower capex. The archetype also serves food-industry refrigeration, which runs most of the year. S97 (capex) is open separately.
benchmark: Process refrigeration about 50-70% (the siblings' 60%); comfort cooling 10-20%.
recommendation: Use one capacity factor across the three chillers, or split the HVAC use into its own archetype. Ask Brad which use the CIMS node carries.

value-in-db: blended: total 0.377 t/t, combustion 0 (identity), energy use 0.69 GJ/t; portland: no total
issue: The blended-cement binder mixes scopes. Its total is cradle-to-gate CO2 per t cement, including clinker (Gielen 1997 slag cement 0.35 and fly-ash cement 0.67; Habert 2010 at 50% clinker 0.377). Its energy use is grinding and drying only (Gielen Table 2.3.9). The Portland binder has no total at all, so the two binders cannot be compared on emissions. The 0.377 central also takes the low-clinker end of a pool that spans slag and fly-ash cements. Combustion is set to zero although 0.4 GJ/t of heat (slag drying) is recorded.
benchmark: If the binder node excludes clinker (CIMS takes clinker from the clinker node), blended-cement emissions-total should be only drying combustion, about 0.02 t/t.
recommendation: Ask Brad which scope the cement binder node takes. If clinker is excluded, set aside the whole-cement totals or move them to a note. If included, give binder_portland-cement the same scope. Treat the 0.4 GJ/t heat as fuel so combustion is computed.

value-in-db: alkali: co2 0.40, co2e 0.053, combustion 0.023, process 0; hydrothermal: co2 0.483, co2e 0.232, combustion 0.103 + process 0.102
issue: The total and its parts come from different sources and disagree by 2-17 times. For alkali-activated binder, the CO2 total pools ETSAP, Worrell, and Gielen (0.3-0.55, some excluding activator production), while the parts and the CO2-eq total are the UKERC E-crete row (tp-nbf_2007_001-0006). For the hydrothermal binder, CSI-ECRA's 0.483 (tp-csi-ecra_2017_001-0116, '57% of clinker') sits against UKERC Celitement at 0.232. MC009 and S121 (alkali-activated energy-use scope) are still live in this build.
benchmark: CO2 should be at or below CO2-eq and equal to combustion + process. Published geopolymer binders run 0.15-0.4 t/t including activator; Celitement claims about 50% below OPC (about 0.4-0.45).
recommendation: Choose one scope per binder (with or without activator production) and set aside the other source's rows. Let id-total-from-parts or the sourced total win consistently. Settle S121 at the same time.

issue: The total equals the steam row only. A separate heat row of 0.619 GJ/t (dairy pasteuriser, tp-giner-santonja_2019_001-0071) and electricity of 0.055 sit outside it, so the carriers sum to 3.2 times the total (screen-carriers). On a steam-heated exchanger, heat and steam are the same duty, and the 2026-10-21 ruling says the total includes every carrier.
benchmark: Total about 0.36 GJ/t (steam 0.31 + electricity 0.05), with the dairy heat figure counted as a steam example.
recommendation: Re-target tp-giner-santonja_2019_001-0071 to steam (or record it as useful heat outside the total) and add electricity to the total.

issue: The methane HHV/LHV factor (1.1096) is applied to all-carrier totals with heating value not stated: cusano_2017_001 nickel totals, van-geene card sums (0557, 0566, 0570), the etsap anode row, cusano homogenizing rows, and the IAI alumina intensities. Where the total includes electricity or coal, the factor inflates the electricity share by 11 % and overstates coal and oil by about 5 %.
benchmark: Apply the factor to the fuel share only, and use the solid or liquid factor for coal or oil; electricity takes none.
recommendation: Restrict cf-hhv-lhv-methane in the normaliser to fuel-only rows, or to the fuel share of an all-carrier total where the example states it; flag the others as basis unknown.

value-in-db: (no row); emissions-process co2e 20.9 t/t is SF6 cover gas only
issue: The Pidgeon retort burns its 70 GJ/t of coal and 50 GJ/t of gas as fuel (ferrosilicon is the reductant), but the fuel-emission-factor identity skips every reactor, so the archetype shows no fuel CO2. recommendation: Allow id-combustion-co2-from-fuel on reactor_silicothermic (its fuel is not a feedstock), add a process CO2 judgement for calcination, and keep SF6 as a species row.

issue: tp-cusano_2017_001-0204 is the overall-process GHG of a nickel heap-leach pilot (species not stated), while the pooled SEC is copper electrowinning (NM004) and emissions-combustion is identity 0. The total is a different metal and a whole-process scope, and it has no parts to sum to.
benchmark: Copper SX-EW direct emissions are small (electricity only, combustion 0); a whole-process nickel figure belongs to no single vessel.
recommendation: Exclude tp-cusano_2017_001-0204 from this archetype (or move it to a nickel route note); leave emissions-total to the identity.

issue: The central is tp-van-geene_2024_001-0558, card TC0220 casting of liquid PRIMARY aluminium, not a scrap remelting furnace, and the total sits below the archetype own combustion identity (0.234 t/t from 4.62 GJ/t of gas).
benchmark: Scrap remelting in reverberatory or rotary furnaces: 0.2-0.37 t CO2/t (van-geene TC0226 0.365; combustion identity 0.234).
recommendation: Exclude tp-van-geene_2024_001-0558 from this archetype (re-map to a casting archetype if one exists); total then follows TC0226 or the identity.

issue: Filled by est-cost-ratio-opex-fixed from a same-equipment pool of only 4 compressors (median 0.698), all methane devices whose opex/capex ratios run 0.2-1.8 because their capex is small and their opex is labour. A flare gas recovery compressor package is ordinary rotating equipment.
benchmark: About 4-8% of capex a year for a packaged compressor (the all-family pool here gives 0.047).
recommendation: Raise the same-equipment min-pool to 5 (as the family and all pools already are) or exclude the methane devices as above.

issue: The central is the median of three pooled rows, two of which are the same CERI 30,000 bbl/d design basis (35,910 GJ/d) reprinted in ceri_2017_001 and ceri_2018_001 (tp-ceri_2017_001-0007-total, tp-ceri_2018_001-0009-total). The new Petrinex row (tp-petrinex_2026_001-0016, 8.84 GJ/m3 HHV, median of 32 operating schemes 2022-2024) is outvoted by one design case counted twice; ceri_2017_002-0008 reprints it a third time on the natural-gas carrier.
benchmark: Operating SAGD schemes use about 230 m3 gas per m3 bitumen (Petrinex 2022-2024), 8.8 GJ/m3 HHV, consistent with SORs of 2.8-3.2.
recommendation: Mark the CERI 2018 and CERI 2017_002 design-basis rows duplicate-of the CERI 2017_001 row, so the pool is one design case plus the Petrinex median; central then about 8.3-8.8 GJ/m3. Check the same CERI reprints on the electricity carrier.

issue: The single row is ceri_2017_002 Table 2.7 'full upgrading benchmark' (tp-ceri_2017_002-0056), 132 kg CO2 per bbl of bitumen feed. It is about twice what the archetype's own energy use implies: 4.16 GJ/m3 of gas (0.21 t) plus hydrogen 2.08 GJ/m3 from SMR (about 0.15 t) gives about 0.36 t/m3. The CERI partial-upgrading note (tp-ceri_2017_002-0087) already says the 132 does not reconcile with the text. The basis is also per bbl of bitumen feed, while the archetype's product is synthetic crude.
benchmark: Upgrading alone about 40-70 kg CO2e per bbl SCO (Englander and Brandt 2014; Suncor and Syncrude upgrader intensities), i.e. 0.25-0.45 t/m3.
recommendation: Ask Brad whether to keep the CERI benchmark; if kept, set it aside or widen the band, and convert per bbl feed to per m3 SCO with the coker liquid yield (about 0.85).

issue: The pool mixes four different partial-upgrading processes from ceri_2017_002 Table 2.7: EJS 3 kg/bbl, CCC 20, HTL 36 (co2) and HI-Q 57 kg CO2e/bbl, the last 'in addition to bitumen extraction'. The co2e is therefore 2.8x the co2, and the central co2 (CCC) is 8x what the archetype's own SEC implies (0.27 GJ/m3 gas plus 0.045 GJ/m3 electricity is about 0.016 t/m3, which matches EJS).
benchmark: Emissions consistent with the archetype's own SEC: about 0.02-0.03 t CO2/m3.
recommendation: Pick one representative process for the archetype (the SEC is EJS) and set the others aside, or split HTL and HI-Q into their own archetypes; drop the HI-Q co2e row or re-scope it.

value-in-db: SEC 5.07 GJ/GJ; co2 0.257 t/GJ; co2e 0.391 t/GJ (band 0.25-0.77)
issue: Every value comes from one vendor study, liberty_2020_001 (a maker of gas-engine fleets), whose field case runs the turbines at 58% daily utilisation with idling (tp-liberty_2020_001-0052). On that basis the electric fleet uses 1.6x the energy and emits 1.7x the CO2e of the diesel fleet (3.21 GJ/GJ, 0.233 t/GJ). The co2e band pools 13 simulated conditions from two figures, so the co2e central sits 50% above the identity CO2 from the same archetype's SEC.
benchmark: Turbine e-fleets at full load run near 30-35% (LHV) gas-to-shaft, about 3.2-3.7 GJ per GJ hydraulic incl. motor losses; grid-tied e-fleets burn nothing on site. Operators' published e-frac reductions are 20-40% versus Tier 2 diesel.
recommendation: Ask Brad whether the archetype is turbine-powered or grid-tied. If turbine, add a second source and keep the Liberty field case as the high; if grid, re-target the SEC to electricity. Take co2e from the same case as the SEC.

issue: The variant still carries the drafted reboiler natural-gas carrier that OG001 rejected on the host (the host's reboiler duty is now sourced heat). The 0.00045 sits outside the variant's total (heat 0.000495 + electricity 3.7e-5 + steam 4.6e-5 = 0.000578), so the carriers sum to 0.00103, and the reboiler is counted twice (heat and gas). Combustion CO2 is 0 although a natural-gas carrier exists.
benchmark: Same carriers as the host plus the capture add-on: total about 0.00058 GJ/m3, no separate gas carrier.
recommendation: Reject the variant's natural-gas fill-judgement row as OG001 did for the host.

issue: Two drafted carriers sit outside the variant's total of 4.54 GJ/m3 (= host electricity, fuel and natural gas plus capture steam and electricity), so the carriers sum to 5.84. The host has neither carrier, so they are either missing from the host or should not be on the variant.

recommendation: Remove the two judgement rows from the variant, or add them to the host and let ccs-host-plus-addon-energy carry them.

issue: Only two rows remain in the pool, epa_2019_001 Table 5-7 break-even prices (tp-epa_2019_001-0177, 685 USD; -0183, 5987 USD per t CO2-eq); the NCCP 1999 and Dunsky 2023 rows (-3 to 108 CAD/t) are ruled out. The co2e central sits above the same archetype's ch4 central (976 CAD per t CH4, about 35 CAD per t CO2-eq), which cannot be; the EPA rows look like per t CH4 or per device, the same mislabel as S73.
