recommendation: Re-read epa_2019_001 Table 5-7 units; if per t CH4 re-target to ch4, otherwise exclude as a break-even price of a different scope.

value-in-db: low-bleed co2 2.03e-6 t/m3; natural-gas 4e-05 GJ/m3 with total not-applicable
issue: The drafted natural-gas carrier on a gas-driven or low-bleed pneumatic is supply gas that the device VENTS, but id-combustion-co2-from-fuel turns it into combustion CO2 on low-bleed (and on plunger lift). Low-bleed has no emissions-process ch4, the quantity that matters. On both pneumatics the total is not-applicable while a carrier row exists.
benchmark: A low-bleed device vents under 6 scf/h (about 0.17 m3/h) by definition, against 0.23-0.97 m3/h for the gas-driven devices in clearstone_2018_001 Table 16, so emissions-process ch4 a fraction of the gas-driven 4.1e-6 t/m3; combustion CO2 zero.
recommendation: Drop the natural-gas carrier judgements on the pneumatics (or re-scope them as emissions-process ch4), add an emissions-process ch4 row on low-bleed, and add pneumatic-device and plunger-lift to the exclude-equipment list of id-combustion-co2-from-fuel.

value-in-db: natural-gas 5.65 GJ/m3; no electricity; co2 0.286 t/m3 gross
issue: The gas use is derived from the SAGD base less 20-30% (tp-ceri_2017_002-0033), but an oxy-fired downhole steam generator also needs an air separation unit, and no electricity carrier is written. The OG011 manual step (re-extract the CERI 0-10 kg CO2e/bbl as a net emissions-total and add emissions-captured) has not been applied, so the archetype still shows the full combustion CO2 although the CO2 stays in the reservoir.
benchmark: About 0.45 t O2 per m3 bitumen at 5.65 GJ gas, at 200-250 kWh/t O2: about 0.3-0.4 GJ/m3 electricity. Net emissions 0-0.063 t CO2e/m3 (CERI 2017).
recommendation: Apply the OG011 re-extraction; add an electricity judgement for the ASU.

issue: The archetype has no energy use at all, only an efficiency of 35% (ipieca_2025_001) and a zero combustion identity. Artificial lift is the largest electricity use in conventional oil production.
benchmark: Rod pumps and ESPs: about 20-60 kWh per m3 of total fluid; at Alberta water cuts about 0.2-0.6 GJ electricity per m3 oil.
recommendation: Add an electricity SEC judgement from lift work (depth x fluid per m3 oil / 0.35), or a sourced row (IPIECA or AER ST60 fuel and power data).

issue: The feed take-off worked (tp-dea_2026_003-0409, 3.448 less 1), but the remaining 2.28 GJ/GJ is the lignin and residue that DEA sheet 106 sends to co-products (power, heat, pellets). The build records no output flow for them, so SEC implies 30 % efficiency while the pooled efficiency is 42 %. The previous pass raised this as PB025, and the build still shows it.
benchmark: Net process energy of a stover biorefinery with lignin export of roughly 0.3-1.2 GJ/GJ (Humbird 2011 1.15 is the whole combustion of the feed).
recommendation: Record DEA's co-product outputs as output flows (per the gross-input ruling) or ask Brad whether the lignin burnt on site counts; re-read Humbird for the boiler fuel only.

issue: The only row is Van Geene 2024 MIDDEN TC0301 (611 EUR/kW-yr), while the capex median of 59.74 comes from eight other sources. The MIDDEN capex for the same card is 315.6, so fixed O&M is 55 % of the pooled capex per year. The backtest and outlier screens flag it (9x the family median).

recommendation: Pool opex-fixed as a ratio to the same source's capex (MIDDEN 611/5820 = 10.5 %), or fill it by est-cost-ratio-opex-fixed instead of the single MIDDEN row.

value-in-db: product-unit t; every other biofuels archetype is GJ
issue: These two archetypes sit on a tonne basis (capex $/t-per-yr, levelized $/t) while the other 21 biofuels archetypes are on GJ, against the one-product-basis-per-family ruling. Their costs cannot be compared with siblings, and the outlier screens rank them as 11-14x outliers for that reason.

NRCan 2008 Table 3-5 gives 0 GJ/ODt for Canadian groundwood mills. The electricity, at 2133-2283 kWh per short ton, sits above NRCan's Canadian median of 1780 kWh/ODt.

recommendation: Re-read the Jacobs and Kramer steam rows for scope; if they cover more than the grinder, exclude them; consider NRCan as the Canadian central.

issue: The variant captures 32 % of the host's 1.112 t/t biogenic CO2, yet reports a 68 % emissions reduction, so the two sourced values do not describe the same plant. A 32 % share is also low for a post-combustion plant on a recovery boiler stack. The steam add-on, about 1.9 GJ/t CO2, is below amine norms.

recommendation: Trace the three share-to-capture rows and pick one scope (stack or mill); set emissions-captured from the 90 % case if that is the design; recheck the steam add-on.

value-in-db: LED capex 13.70 CAD/Mlm-h-per-yr, opex-fixed 0.472; T12 capex 2.35, opex 0.112; levelized incl. energy LED 6.09 vs T12 2.15 and T8 2.27

issue: Oxy-fuel regeneration is a capture route (the archetype is quantified from Gudde 2019 and IEAGHG 2017 refinery retrofit cases), but it carries no emissions rows, captured CO2, or capture share, unlike reactor_fluid-catalytic-cracking_ccs-diffuse. recommendation: Treat it as a capture variant: add share-to-capture and the ccs-host-emissions identities, or rename it _ccs-oxy-fuel so the variant rules pick it up.

issue: The SEC guess borrows from heat-pump_space (its rationale still uses the pre-rename name), so free evaporative cooling gets a chiller's COP. Free cooling needs only fans and pumps. The lifetime low of 1 year comes from est-class-lifetime measure lives (OT023, still present).

recommendation: Re-guess SEC at about 0.04 GJ/GJ, floor the lifetime band at 10 years, and update the stale archetype names in the guess text.

issue: Brewery and dairy rows stated per volume are excluded with 'no conversion from GJ/m3 (kWh/m3, MJ/hl) to GJ/t'.
